claims_disputed.claim: Code-X 27B reaches 43.3% on OmniGAIA and 60.0% on LVOmniBench, SOTA among open-source models.
claims_disputed.reason: Table 4 (§3.3) has only an SFT row for Qwen3.6-27B (43.3 OmniGAIA avg, 60.0 LVOmniBench avg). There is no 27B RL row, so the review's evidence ('27B RL model') is wrong and GSPO is shown only at 9B. 'SOTA among open-source' rests on one open-source comparator, OmniAtlas-Omni-30B-A3B (20.8 / 34.0), plus the untrained Qwen bases. The 27B Direct MLLM baseline already reaches 38.2 / 51.0. OmniCoding training data includes OmniGAIA-SFT-2K, the supervised subset distributed with the OmniGAIA eval (§3.1, App. dataset list), so the OmniGAIA gain is in-distribution. All results are single-run pass@1.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: With the same GPT-5.4 High controller, Codex trails OmniAgent on OmniGAIA (61.4 vs 66.4) and SocialOmni L2 Q1 (51 vs 56), and leads on SocialOmni L1, LVOmniBench and VideoZeroBench (Table 1). OmniAgent ran with 'External web and code tools ... disabled' and used Qwen2.5-Omni-7B for video (App. H.3.2), while Codex had web search, package installs and GPT-5.4 vision (§2 Environments). Code-as-action is therefore not isolated from web access or perception-model strength. Against native models, Gemini 3.1 Pro still leads LVOmniBench and SocialOmni L1 (§2.1). Wins are real but benchmark-dependent and confounded.

The Ubuntu workspace is simply the evaluation environment (§2 Environments). No unsandboxed or differently isolated arm exists, and the review's own note says there is no security evaluation. The system uses sandboxing without measuring it.

Skills beat No Skills on one model and effort level in single runs (Table 13 / Fig. 7: 61.4 → 70.5 / 73.0 / 76.7). However, the self-evolved artifacts are one '# Agent Guide' markdown (App. H.2 prompts), and on-demand loading versus always-in-context is never described or isolated. The calibration prompt asks the writer to compare against 'OmniGAIA reference answer processes' (Fig. 12) and evaluation is on OmniGAIA, with no held-out split. The no-skill baseline (High, 61.4) is also below the no-skill xHigh run (75.0).

The retag premise 'same GPT-5.4-high backbone' is false. Agent-Omni's video and audio agents are local Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, all agents run at temperature 0 with max_tokens 4096, and max_round_num is 2 (App. H.3.1). Against OmniAgent, which runs 30 iterations at temperature 1 with gpt-4o-audio, budget and models differ, and Agent-Omni even wins LVOmniBench (36 vs 33). The static-graph variable is never isolated, so the paper does not measure P36.

missed_issues: other:handicapped_baselines: the scaffold baselines had web and code tools disabled (OmniAgent, App. H.3.2) and delegated video perception to Qwen2.5-Omni-7B (both scaffolds; Agent-Omni also uses it for audio), while the coding agents had web search, package installs and GPT-5.4 vision. The review's verdict_reason calls these 'strong, current baselines' without noting this.

Table 1 does not say whether native omni models had tools or web search on OmniGAIA, which §2 describes as 'tool-mediated factual and multi-hop'. 'Beats Gemini 3.1 Pro (66.1)' may therefore compare a web-enabled agent with a closed-book model. Only the Table 4 caption says Direct MLLM baselines got tools.

The review's P33 note says the coding agent beats scaffolds 'on tool-oriented benchmarks'. On OmniGAIA, the most tool-oriented benchmark, OmniAgent beats Codex at matched effort (66.4 vs 61.4); Codex wins there only at xHigh.

no_variance_reported is understated. Run-to-run noise is visible: text-only GPT-5.4 High (64.4 OmniGAIA) beats the vision run (61.4), and LVOmniBench is non-monotonic in effort (High 58 vs xHigh 57). Skill gains of 9–15 pp from single runs on 360 items need repeats.

TerminalBench-O pass rate is flat across GPT-5.5 effort (Low = High = xHigh = 24%, i.e. 12/50; Medium 18%) while the average score moves 0.68 → 0.71 (Table 5). The ≥70 threshold plus zero-on-gating-failure rule (§4) likely dominates. No Claude model was evaluated on it.

GSPO RL is shown only at 9B (OmniGAIA 23.1 → 28.1, LVOmniBench 33 → 53 vs SFT). The 27B result is SFT-only. P25 supports still holds via 9B RL and via SFT beating the untrained bases, but the review's P25 note implies RL at both scales.

Acknowledgments say the first author is supported by Modal, Tavily (a web-search API; agents use web_search) and Linear. The review says no acknowledgments were extracted. None of these products is evaluated, so this is at most coi_risk 1 / low, but it should be recorded.
note: Same verdict (admit_with_caveats), but the review's harness stances overstate the evidence. The coding-agent-vs-scaffold wins pit a web-enabled Codex against scaffolds with web and code disabled and 7B perception models, and the new P36 'contradicts' tag rests on a false 'same backbone' premise. The 27B headline is an SFT result, not RL, and its OmniGAIA gain is in-distribution.
